comparisons.peer_topic: Redemption Rights and Depositary Share Structures
comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation may redeem most preferred stock series at its option at liquidation preference plus unpaid dividends, except for Series B and Series L which lack early redemption rights. Ownership is generally held via depositary shares representing fractional interests in preferred stock, with dividend payment frequencies and minimum rates varying by series as detailed in the table footnotes.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America disclose that their preferred stock series are issued as depositary shares representing fractional interests and that dividends are paid quarterly, if declared by the Board. Citi’s Series X pays dividends at a fixed rate until February 18, 2026, thereafter resetting to the five-year treasury rate plus a spread; similarly, Bank of America notes that certain series (e.g., Series B and L in footnotes) pay quarterly cash dividends if and when declared, with some series adjusting to quarterly payments upon specific dates.

comparisons.peer_topic: 2025 Issuance of Series Z Preferred Stock
comparisons.peer_summary: In January 2025, the firm issued 76,000 shares of Series Z 6.85% Fixed-Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock, which has a $25,000 liquidation preference, is redeemable at the firm's option starting February 10, 2030, and pays semi-annual dividends at 6.85% per annum until that date, thereafter resetting to 2.461% plus the five-year treasury rate.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Goldman Sachs disclose the issuance of new Fixed-Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock Series with specific fixed-rate periods followed by resets to a treasury-based floating rate. Citigroup’s Series X (issued prior to 2024 but active in 2024) resets to the five-year treasury rate plus 3.417% after February 18, 2026. Goldman Sachs’ Series Z, issued in January 2025, pays a fixed 6.85% until February 10, 2030, thereafter resetting to 2.461% plus the five-year treasury rate. Both utilize depositary shares and have similar non-cumulative dividend structures.

sentences.text: (9)Issued as depositary shares, each representing a 1/25th interest in a share of the corresponding series of non-cumulative perpetual preferred stock.

Dividends are payable quarterly on February 18, May 18, August 18 and November 18 at a fixed rate until, but excluding, February 18, 2026, thereafter payable quarterly on the same dates at a fixed rate that resets on the Series X reset date and every five years thereafter equal to the five-year treasury rate plus 3.417%, in each case when, as and if declared by the Citi Board of Directors.

Each share of Series Z Preferred Stock issued and outstanding has a liquidation preference of $25,000 per share, is represented by 25 depositary shares and is redeemable at the firm's option beginning February 10, 2030 at a redemption price equal to $25,000 per share plus declared and unpaid dividends.

Dividends on Series Z Preferred Stock, if declared, are payable semi-annually at (i) 6.85% per annum from the issuance date to, but excluding, February 10, 2030 and, thereafter, (ii) 2.461% per annum plus the five-year treasury rate.

comparisons.peer_topic: Preferred Stock Dividend Policy and Reference Rates
comparisons.peer_summary: Dividends are discretionary, non-cumulative, and declared quarterly. Fixed-to-floating rate preferred stock uses SOFR or CMT as reference rates following the transition from LIBOR, with specific spread adjustments defined.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and JPMorgan Chase disclose that their preferred stock dividends are non-cumulative and payable only when declared. Citigroup’s Series X dividends are payable quarterly when declared by the Citi Board. JPMorgan’s disclosures confirm that dividends on its non-cumulative preferred stock are discretionary and declared quarterly, with fixed-to-floating rates transitioning after initial periods. Both firms use treasury-based reference rates (Citi uses five-year treasury; JPM uses CMT which is also a treasury-based rate) for the floating portion of the dividends.

comparisons.peer_summary: Series M preferred stock dividends are payable semiannually until September 15, 2026, and quarterly thereafter.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Morgan Stanley disclose specific payment frequency schedules for their preferred stock series that transition from a fixed rate or frequency to a different one after a set date. Citigroup’s Series X pays quarterly fixed dividends until February 18, 2026, then resets. Morgan Stanley’s Series M pays semiannually until September 15, 2026, and quarterly thereafter. Both companies explicitly define the transition dates and frequencies in their notes.
